critical_code_review_comments: FIXED: CourseDetail.jsx used `useEffect(load, [code])` (3 occurrences in CourseDetail/DevoirPanel/ForumPanel) where `load` returned a Promise from axios .then chain. In React 19 this triggers runtime error 'destroy is not a function' (the Promise is interpreted as cleanup fn). Changed to `useEffect(() => { load(); }, [code])`. This caused Forum tab (and progress reload) to crash the SPA.

`DevoirPanel.grade` uses native `window.prompt()` — works but is poor UX; replace with a modal + inputs.

rca of the issue: Issue: Opening a course and switching to Forum/Devoir tab, or submitting a devoir, crashed the SPA with runtime error 'destroy is not a function' from react-dom-client. Repro: login as any user → navigate to /cours/SW10 → click Forum tab. RCA: `useEffect(load, [code])` was passed the `load` function directly, but `load` returns `api.get(...).then(...)` which is a Promise. React 19 strictly expects the effect to return either `undefined` or a cleanup function; it tries to invoke `.destroy()` or treat the returned value as a cleanup, causing the crash on re-render / tab switch. Mitigation: wrap in arrow function so the effect returns undefined: `useEffect(() => { load(); }, [code])`. Applied to 3 call sites in /app/frontend/src/pages/CourseDetail.jsx.
